questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My main objective of going on exchange was to explore new cultures and experiencing what it was like living abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I would say. I received info on mail in good time before arrival, and the host university were quick to respond if I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were an introduction day for incoming exchange students the week before semester start. Everything about your courses and exchange-related activities were explained, along with a tour of the campus. You also get assigned a "buddy", who you can contact if you have further questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not too easy, I found an apartment on a random site called flatio, but I think the safest bet is either idealista or maybe try and see if you can join the whatsapp groups for exchange students in Bilbao. There seemed to be some rooms offered in those groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of good places to live in Bilbao, and most of them are close to a metro station that goes straight to the campus at Sarriko. I can recommend areas like Indautxu, Abando, Casco Viejo (they are probably the most expensive though). I would personally avoid living in San Francisco as it seemed as a dodgy neighborhood.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't think the host university helped providing any housing as I recall.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the courses on the website after a good amount of looking. The courses are split up into 5 blocks to avoid overlapping between the courses you pick.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Once again the help was good. I asked them if the courses I found were the correct ones, because it looked like it was the previous year. But they confirmed it was the correct courses I was picking from.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted but one, which was cancelled for some reason. That meant I had to pick another course and since I couldn't get any other courses from that block pre approved by UCPH, I had to pick a course that overlapped with another course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get your pre approval from UCPH in good time to be sure you can get a course from each block approved, to avoid overlapping.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied quite a lot from course to course. Some were really easy, partly because I was a masters student and some parts of the courses were closely related to something I had learned earlier. Others were quite hard, especially because the exam is without any notes and has to be handwritten.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching almost felt closer to high school than university since a minimum attendance were required for each course to be approved for the continuous evaluation. However, it is possible to decide not to take part in the continuous evaluation and only be evaluated on your exam. I wouldn't recommend this, since I failed my first try at both exams where I hadn't been attending the course regularly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban Economics
Economics of Development
Public Sector Economics - Spending
Financial Accounting
Applications of Marketing Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For academic reasons I would recommend Economics of Development, for a more chilled and easy (but still interesting) course I would recommend Urban Economics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say I experienced any major unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating and drinking at bars and restaurants were cheaper relatively to grocery shopping compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some activities, but they weren't organised by the university but by some exchange student organizations like ESN or Happy Erasmus. I didn't really attend it though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out and eat some pintxos and drink a glass of txakoli at some of the local taberna, especially in Casco Viejo. Visit Guggenheim.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to watch a game at San Mames if you're interested in football. Also go out explore the nature and the other cities of the Basque Country and maybe even walk a couple days on the Camino. Busses to other cities like Santander or San Sebastian are fairly cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Only thing was that they eat a lot later then in Denmark, so many restaurants aren't open until 20 or later. Also a lot of shops, including supermarkets, are closed on sundays. So you need to prepare for that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really that much to be honest, the only thing would be that language barrier. But most of them spoke a little bit of English and I spoke some Spanish so it was not a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love that they use the city a lot. There are always people in the street and they love to go out for just a little bit of food or a glass of wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The choices of courses isn't the greatest if you are a masters student since a lot of them cant be approved by UCPH.
Bilbao is a lovely and cheap city to live in.
Go to the classes, or the exams will be very hard. You don't get access to previous exam sets and solutions.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the experience of living abroad and getting to explore Bilbao and the rest of the Basque Country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams for the courses that I hadn't been attending.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
